brief: Signs and verifies requests between nodes and webhook bodies with HMAC-SHA256, refusing forged, stale and replayed ones.
detail: Governance decides whether a caller may proceed; signing proves the request is from that caller and was not altered. Each caller key id shares a secret with the receiver. Sign computes an HMAC-SHA256 over a length-prefixed canonical form of the method, path, body, timestamp and nonce; Verify recomputes it and also demands a fresh timestamp and a nonce not used before, remembered for the freshness window. The comparison is constant-time through a double HMAC. A second form, SignBody, VerifyBody and VerifyWebhook, covers a webhook that signs only its raw body, and tries every held key so that an old and a new secret can overlap. Every refusal returns a reason and is noted in the process security ledger when one is open, with the caveats written on Verify. Secrets in examples here are invented.
